data.name: The Clockwork Man
data.detailed_description:
Explora uma fantástica visão da era Vitoriana em The Clockwork Man, um épico jogo de objetos-ocultos. Ao virar do século, numa linha de tempo alternativa, a tecnologia a vapor demonstrou-se dominante em quase todas as profissões.

A mais recente numa longa linha de engenheiros e inventores, Miranda Calomy teve sempre um dom especial para solucionar problemas de forma criativa. Quando uma estranha carta do seu avô chega ao seu apartamento em Londres, Miranda põe de lado os seus planos e embarca numa aventura global. Conseguirá ela juntar todas as peças da maior invenção do mundo antes que seja demasiado tarde?

Junta-te a Miranda e Sprocket numa incrível jornada de desafios de objetos ocultos e quebra-cabeças intrigantes num cenário Steampunk.

Principais características:

  • Deslumbrantes cenários com a possibilidade de aproximar e arrastar
  • Centenas de itens da era Vitoriana pintados à mão
  • Aventura & puzzles lógicos
  • Um inovador sistema de dicas: Sprocket, o Robô!
  • Joga os teus níveis favoritos quantas vezes quiseres em modo Freeplay
  • A posição dos objetos muda em cada novo jogo
  • Banda sonora atmosférica e dobragem

reviews.review:
Valve, please. Just give us one more option besides a "yes" or a "no". A half-hearted "mneh" or a a shrug icon or even a thumb pointing sideways.

Because that's how I feel about The Clockwork Man. Not angry or frustrated enough to condemn this hidden object game, but not impressed enough to turn my thumbs upwards either.

There're certainly some aspects to praise about the game. It comes with a fairly unique hint system, built into the game's clockwork sidekick. It uses charges to help the player find more difficult objects, and recharges slowly over time so it doesn't make the game too easy all at once. The art is nice at least, and the game is mildly spiced up with other kinds of puzzles in-between hidden-object-finding sessions.

On the other hand, there just isn't much else to the game. I finished in about two hours, with some help from the hint system. The puzzles are nice, but they're also obvious (and overdone) to the seasoned puzzler. Upon completion, The Clockwork Man offers a freeplay mode, but those are for Hidden Object maps that you've already played by then.

The biggest disappointment had to be the setting. It promised an alternate-history steampowered Victorian world, and it delivered that in the first few moments. But then you're sent to an under-developed tropical island where little to none of that ever comes into play. Your "global" adventure only consists of a few moments in your Victorian home and the rest of it on a single generic tropical mystery-island. The only steampowered clockwork wonders you'll experience are your sidekick Sprocket and [spoiler]what you discover during the short finale[/spoiler].

Hidden Object game enthusiasts will like this more, but they'd be better off with The Clockwork Man Bundle, which consists of this game and its sequel (which appears to at least have more Victorian steampunk elements). For everyone else though, whatever the second game is like, I can definitely say that The Clockwork Man is underwhelming and not worth a full-price purchase.
